Thank you for taking an interest in Drybrook school. The school is situated in the heart of the Forest of Dean in an area of outstanding natural beauty.
Drybrook is part of the Forest of Dean Trust which enables us to work with our local community and wider stakeholders to create the best possible environment for learning that we can. Our curriculum is tailored to meet the needs of the children that we serve, raising their aspirations and allowing them to pursue their dreams, with a particular emphasis on excellence and enjoyment. We listen, challenge and support each other while recognising that we all develop at a different pace and all experience a different journey. Our community continues to thrive because of the relentless focus that we have on excellent teaching and learning. At Drybrook we really do ‘dream big and achieve together'.

Values and Ethos
Statement of Values and Ethos At Drybrook Primary School, our vision is Dreaming Big, Achieving Together. We are committed to nurturing every student’s potential in a supportive and collaborative environment, fostering an educational experience that helps each child excel academically, socially, and emotionally. This ethos is reflected in our daily practice and the core beliefs that underpin our approach to education. Our Core Values: • Respect and Kindness: We promote an environment of mutual respect and kindness where students are encouraged to appreciate and learn from the diverse perspectives of others. Our community is built on positive relationships, where everyone feels valued and supported. • Excellence and Achievement: We believe in equipping every pupil with the knowledge, skills, and confidence needed to succeed. Students leave Drybrook Primary School with strong foundations in literacy, numeracy, and critical thinking, ready to embrace future challenges with resilience and ambition. • Safety and Well-being: The well-being of our students is at the heart of our ethos. We provide a safe, inclusive, and nurturing environment where children can grow, thrive, and develop a strong sense of self-esteem and self-worth. • Responsibility and Resilience: We encourage students to take responsibility for their actions and develop the resilience needed to overcome challenges. By embedding the values of respect, readiness, and safety into daily routines, we ensure students are prepared to engage fully in their learning journey. • Collaboration and Community: At Drybrook, students, staff, and families work together to foster an inclusive and supportive school community. We encourage collective success through teamwork and shared responsibility, ensuring every child has the opportunity to flourish. Ethos: Our ethos is rooted in a deep commitment to helping students dream big and achieve their potential. We believe that fostering a love for learning, combined with high expectations, mutual respect, and positive relationships, equips our pupils with the skills and resilience they need to navigate the future confidently. Through the core belief that education is more than just academic achievement, we aim to develop well-rounded, confident, and respectful individuals who can make positive contributions to society. We encourage creativity, critical thinking, and adaptability, ensuring our students are prepared for life’s challenges. Underpinning Educational Beliefs: The following four educational beliefs guide all aspects of teaching and learning at Drybrook Primary School: • Be Literate: Literacy is the foundation for all learning. We believe in fostering strong reading and writing skills that allow students to engage with the world around them, communicate effectively, and pursue lifelong learning. • Be Numerate: Numeracy is essential for problem-solving and critical thinking. We aim to develop students' numerical abilities, enabling them to tackle both everyday tasks and complex challenges with confidence. • Have the Ability to Think: We nurture critical and creative thinking skills in our students, encouraging them to analyze, question, and understand the world. Developing independent thinkers prepares our students to innovate and adapt in an ever-changing world. • Generate Positive Self-Esteem and Self-Image: We believe that emotional well-being is key to success. By promoting positive self-esteem and a healthy self-image, we empower our students to be resilient, confident, and ready to overcome setbacks with determination. School Aims: • Inspiring Excellence: We inspire every student to aim high and achieve their potential, equipping them with the confidence and skills needed to succeed academically and personally. • Empowering Independent Learners: We nurture independence and critical thinking, ensuring every child leaves us with the ability to think critically and creatively about the world around them. • Promoting Well-being: We provide a supportive and safe environment where students can develop positive relationships, grow in self-esteem, and achieve emotional well-being. • Building a Strong Community: We foster a collaborative school community where students, staff, and families work together to support and inspire one another, ensuring collective growth and success. • Preparing for the Future: We prepare our students for the next stages of their education and life beyond school, encouraging them to embrace challenges with resilience and a love for lifelong learning.

Drybrook Methodist Church
Children and Young People
Drybrook Methodist Church runs regular school holiday activities for children and young people, including Lego Cafe, Pop Up Sports, and a very messy Gingerbread House building workshop at Christmas! During the week the building hosts CANDI YouthSpace every Tuesday, and a team from the church enjoys visiting Drybrook school for story-telling assemblies. A monthly children's church called 'KickStart' is held jointly with the Methodist church at Bailey Lane End. Other Activities A popular coffee morning (with Bring and Buy) runs for the local community on the first Saturday of every month. Sunday services are weekly at 11am, with a programme of events and activities running regularly alongside it. Welcome
Nurturing Young Minds and Fostering a Love for Learning
At Willow Nursery, part of Drybrook Primary School, we are devoted to nurturing children aged 2 to 4 years in an environment that inspires a love for learning. Our approach to education encompasses all facets of the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) curriculum, ensuring a holistic learning experience for our youngest pupils.
A Rich and Supportive Learning Environment
Our team of dedicated educators crafts high-quality opportunities for play, exploration, and learning. We provide a blend of indoor and outdoor environments, where children can develop their social, emotional, cognitive, and physical skills through hands-on experiences and guided activities. Our inclusive and supportive setting is designed to meet the needs of every child, fostering their growth and development.
Laying Foundations for Literacy and Multicultural Awareness
At Willow Nursery, we are proud of our comprehensive literacy programme. Utilising the Read Write Inc reading scheme, we lay the groundwork for essential literacy skills. Additionally, our Spanish lessons introduce basic language concepts, enriching children's cultural understanding and broadening their global perspective.
Seamless Transition to Primary Education
We recognise the significance of transitioning to primary school and provide tailored support to ensure children are well-prepared for this important milestone. Being part of Drybrook School, our nursery children benefit from a seamless transition into reception, providing a strong start to their educational journey.
Engaging with Families
With an open-door policy, regular updates through Tapestry, and communication via Dojo, we keep parents closely involved in their child's progress and experiences. This partnership with families is integral to our approach.
Celebrating Individuality and Progress
Each child at Willow Nursery is celebrated for their unique strengths, interests, and achievements. Our curriculum supports their progression, laying a solid foundation for lifelong learning and success.
Flexible Options for Families
Willow Nursery offers flexibility to families, accepting both the 15 and 30 hours funding schemes and participating in the tax-free childcare program.
Our hourly rate is £6.50, with session times being AM from 8:40 am to 12 pm, PM from 12 pm to 3:15 pm, or a full day option.
Enriching Indoor and Outdoor Learning Spaces
Our indoor environment includes sensory play, maths exercises, and imaginative play areas, while our outdoor decking area features a sandpit, water tray, and mud kitchen. The larger playground, field, and forest school area provide endless opportunities for physical activity and nature exploration.
Dedicated Key Workers
Each child is assigned a key worker, who plays a crucial role in building strong relationships with the child and family, providing personalised care, and monitoring progress. This close connection ensures that every child's unique needs and interests are catered to, while also supporting and engaging with parents.
At Willow Nursery, we offer an inviting, nurturing space where every child can thrive, explore, and grow, setting the stage for a lifetime of learning and discovery.

We believe in providing a motivating, inclusive, and responsive environment where children can thrive through child-led, open-ended play. Our goal is to foster a lifelong love for learning, respect, confidence, resilience, and curiosity.

Safeguarding & Pastoral Care
At Drybrook Primary School, the safety, welfare and wellbeing of every child are at the heart of everything we do.
Safeguarding is everyone’s responsibility. All staff have an important role in identifying concerns, listening to children and ensuring that children and families receive the right help at the right time. Our approach is child-centred and guided by what is in the best interests of each child.
All staff receive safeguarding and child protection training appropriate to their role, with regular updates throughout the year. Staff are trained to recognise when a child may need help or protection and know that concerns must be acted upon without delay.
Our safeguarding arrangements are supported by our Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy, which is available on the Policies page of this website.
Our Safeguarding Team
Thomas Henesey, Designated Safeguarding Lead
Claire Tuffley, Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead
Donna Hull, Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead
Jade Davies, Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead
Paula Harding, Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead
Children can speak to any trusted adult in school if they are worried about themselves or somebody else.
Parents, carers and members of the community are encouraged to contact us if they have a concern about a child’s safety or wellbeing.
Email: safeguarding@dbp.fodt.co.uk Telephone: 01594 542448
Alternatively, contact the school office and ask to speak to a member of the Safeguarding Team.
If you believe that a child is in immediate danger, call 999.
Reporting a Concern
We take all concerns about children seriously, however small they may initially appear.
Staff must report safeguarding concerns promptly in line with the school’s procedures. Concerns are recorded securely and reviewed by the safeguarding team. Staff must never assume that somebody else will take action.
Where needed, the school works with Children’s Social Care, Family Help, health services, the police and other agencies to make sure children and families receive appropriate support and protection.
Children should know that they can talk to us. If a child is worried about something, they can speak to any adult they trust in school. We will listen, take them seriously and help them get the support they need.
Family Help
Sometimes children and families experience difficulties and need some additional support. Family Help means offering support as soon as a problem emerges, rather than waiting until difficulties become more serious.
This may include support with:
family relationships or changes in family circumstances;
emotional wellbeing or mental health;
attendance or difficulties coming to school;
behaviour or changes in behaviour;
housing, financial difficulties or poverty;
bereavement or loss;
substance or alcohol misuse within the family;
SEND or additional needs;
caring responsibilities;
exploitation or risks outside the home; or
any other issue affecting a child’s wellbeing, development or ability to thrive.
Families do not need to wait until things become extremely difficult before asking for help. A conversation with the school’s safeguarding team is often the best place to start.
Depending on the needs of the child or family, support may include advice and practical help from school, pastoral support, attendance support, SEND support, signposting to local services, Family Help, coordinated work with other professionals, or referral to specialist services where this is needed.
Our aim is always to work with families and alongside other professionals so that children receive the help they need at the right time.

Curriculum and Learning
Our Drybrook Curriculum Intent
At Drybrook Primary School, we understand the significance of fostering dreams and achieving collectively. Our commitment to education is deeply rooted in our core beliefs. We firmly believe that upon leaving Primary school, every child should:
1. Be literate. 2. Be numerate. 3. Possess the ability to think critically. 4. Discover and cultivate a positive self-esteem and self-image.
With these foundational beliefs, our students are immersed in a learning environment that prepares them for the ever-evolving world. They are taught the values of resilience, creativity, and a growth mindset. We emphasise that challenges are a natural part of the learning process, and we nurture our students to face them head-on, adapt, and grow.
Our curriculum is expansive, reflecting our unwavering commitment to laying strong foundations and promoting academic excellence. We operate on the principle that good teaching, rooted in formative assessment and retrieval practice, is paramount. Precise assessment, targeted teaching to bridge any gaps, and a fresh perspective on ability are integral to our approach. Our curriculum is planned to be progressive and sequenced to ensure our students know more, do more, and remember more.
Every day, we inspire our students to challenge themselves, take calculated risks, learn from their setbacks, and persistently work towards their most ambitious aspirations. We encourage them to aim high, all while cherishing their childhood and benefiting from a plethora of diverse opportunities and experiences.
Our curriculum and teaching methods have been tailored to meet the unique needs of our students. We prioritise rapid and effective teaching of reading, writing, and mathematical skills, starting from each child's individual baseline. Our expectations remain high for every student. We emphasise context-rich vocabulary to support all learners, especially those with SEND and EAL. Through clear retrieval and instructional practices, we aim to ensure that learning solidifies, building lasting neural pathways and schemas in the long-term memory.
In essence, our curriculum at Drybrook Primary School aims to: • Provide an environment where every student can learn, succeed, and make significant progress. • Equip students with the knowledge and skills to know more, remember more, and do more. • Prepare our students for subsequent educational stages and their roles in society. • Offer a curriculum that evaluates progress and caters to both academic and emotional needs.
Our Drybrook Curriculum Implementation
At Drybrook Primary School, our curriculum's implementation is as crucial as its intent. We believe that the method and manner in which we deliver our curriculum play a pivotal role in the learning outcomes of our students.
At the heart of our teaching lies a deep understanding of pedagogy – the method and practice of teaching. We recognise that the way concepts are imparted and grasped is fundamental to effective learning. Drawing inspiration from renowned educational research, such as Barak Rosenshine’s Principles of Instruction, we have established a framework for Effective Teaching Practice at Drybrook. This approach enables our students to delve deeper into their learning processes, fostering critical thinking and comprehension.
Evidence-Led Approaches:
Our commitment to excellence in teaching is rooted in evidence-led approaches. Every subject taught at Drybrook is backed by pedagogy, ensuring that our lessons are not just informative but also effective in fostering deep understanding. We continuously engage with the latest research in the Science of Learning, ensuring that our teaching methods are aligned with proven strategies that enhance learning outcomes.
Continuous Professional Development:
Recognising that the quality of teaching directly impacts student success, we invest heavily in the continuous professional development (CPD) of our staff. All team members are routinely engaged in school improvement activities, focusing on refining pedagogy and ensuring that subject content is expertly delivered. This commitment extends to individualised mentoring and coaching, supporting continuous improvements in practice. Our responsive coaching approach ensures that every educator is equipped with the knowledge and tools needed to optimise learning opportunities for all student groups.
The implementation of our curriculum at Drybrook Primary School is a dynamic process, continuously evolving and adapting based on research, feedback, and the unique needs of our students. We are committed to delivering an education that is not only comprehensive in content but also exceptional in delivery.

Drybrook Rugby Club

- Mini Rugby (Ages 3-11): The club offers training for various age groups within the minis, each led by dedicated and skilled coaches. From the youngest "Kittens" group to the under-11s, there's a place for every young rugby enthusiast to start their journey. - Junior Rugby (Ages 12-17): As players grow, so do the challenges and excitement! The junior rugby program continues to nurture and develop skills for older children, preparing them for more competitive play.
- Sunday Mornings: The club's vibrant community gathers every Sunday morning for training and junior matches. It's a great time for kids to learn, play, and make new friends.
- Contact for More Information: To learn more about the club or to join, parents can reach out to the Mini/Junior Lead, Jason Roberts, at 07849020562 or via email at jason.roberts15@sky.com. - Club Location and Contact: The club is based in the heart of the community and welcomes enquiries at info@drybrookrfc.com or 01594 542595.
Drybrook Rugby Club is not just about playing rugby; it's about being part of a community. The club's emphasis on sportsmanship, teamwork, and personal development makes it a great choice for young athletes. Whether your child is new to rugby or looking to enhance their skills, Drybrook Rugby Club offers a supportive and fun environment to do so.
For more information about the club and its activities, you can visit their official website and main page.

SEND and Inclusion
At Drybrook Primary School we recognise that all children have a right to a broad, balanced relevant and differentiated curriculum. We aim to create a happy, educationally exciting and positive environment in which all pupils can develop to their full potential. We recognise that children are individuals and that each child has needs unique to him or her.
We Aim To:
Ensure that our curriculum is responsive to all children whatever their individual need
Promote positive attitudes and individual confidence
Ensure all children experience success
Identify, assess, record and regularly review pupils' special educational needs
Encourage parents/guardians to be involved in planning and supporting at all stages of their child's development using person-centred planning
Make effective use of support services
The Gloucestershire County Council Local Offer for Children with SEN and disabilities can be found here: https://www.glosfamiliesdirectory.org.uk/kb5/gloucs/glosfamilies/family.page?familychannel=2
Definition of SEND
A child has a learning disability if he or she:
Has a significantly greater difficulty in learning than the majority of others of the same age, or
Has a disability which prevents or hinders him or her from making use of educational facilities of a kind generally provided for others of the same age in mainstream schools.
(Code of Practice DfE 2014)

Welcome to Drybrook
We are delighted that you are considering Drybrook Primary School for your child.
Choosing a school is an important decision, and we warmly encourage prospective families to visit us, meet our staff and children, and experience Drybrook for themselves.
Drybrook Primary School is part of the Forest of Dean Trust. The Trust is the admission authority for the school, and the school’s admission arrangements are set out in the policies available at the bottom of this page. As an academy trust, Forest of Dean Trust is required to comply with the statutory School Admissions Code.
If you would like to arrange a visit to Drybrook or have any questions about joining the school, please contact the school office. We will be very happy to help.
Starting School in Reception
Children normally start primary school in September of the school year in which they turn five.
Applications for Reception places are coordinated by Gloucestershire County Council. Parents must apply to the County Council rather than directly to Drybrook Primary School. An application must be made even if your child already attends a nursery or pre-school connected with a particular school, or has an older brother or sister attending the school.
Parents are encouraged to use all their available preferences and list schools in their genuine order of preference. All applications submitted by the closing date are treated equally, regardless of when they are submitted during the application window.
Applications and full information are available through Gloucestershire County Council School Admissions.
Joining Drybrook During the School Year
Applications for children joining Drybrook outside the normal Reception admissions round are known as in-year applications.
This may include children who:
have moved into Drybrook or the surrounding area;
have moved from another part of the country;
are transferring from another school; or
need a school place for another reason during the academic year.
In Gloucestershire, in-year applications are made directly to the school. Gloucestershire County Council does not coordinate in-year admissions.
How to Apply for an In-Year Place
Parents and carers wishing to apply for an in-year place should:
download and complete the Gloucestershire In-Year Application Form below, or collect a copy from the school office;
send the completed form directly to Drybrook Primary School for consideration; and
receive the outcome in writing.
Gloucestershire’s current procedure states that schools should notify parents of the outcome of an in-year application within 10 to 15 school days.
Completed forms can be sent to:
Drybrook Primary School Drybrook Road Drybrook Gloucestershire GL17 9JF
Email: admin@dbp.fodt.co.uk
Further guidance is available from Gloucestershire County Council.
What Happens if a Year Group is Full?
Where Drybrook has places available, applications will be considered in accordance with the school’s published admission arrangements.
Where there are more applications than places available, places must be allocated in accordance with the published oversubscription criteria in the relevant Admissions Policy.
If we are unable to offer your child a place, we will write to explain the decision and provide information about your right of appeal. Gloucestershire County Council can also provide advice about other schools that may have places available.
For further advice about in-year admissions, contact Gloucestershire County Council’s In-Year Admissions Team:
Telephone: 01452 426015 Email: inyear.admissions@gloucestershire.gov.uk
Admission Appeals
Parents and carers have a statutory right of appeal if their application for a school place is refused.
Appeals are heard by an independent appeal panel. The panel is independent of the school and the admission authority. If a place cannot be offered, we will explain how to submit an appeal and the relevant timetable.
Further information about admission appeals is available from Gloucestershire County Council.
Admission Outside a Child’s Normal Age Group
Parents may request that their child is admitted to a year group outside their normal age group.
Any request will be considered in accordance with the School Admissions Code and the school’s published admission arrangements. Decisions are made on the individual circumstances of the case and in the child’s best interests.
Parents considering such a request are encouraged to contact the school so that we can discuss their child’s circumstances.
Children with an Education, Health and Care Plan
The admission arrangements above are different for children with an Education, Health and Care Plan.
Where Drybrook Primary School is named in a child’s Education, Health and Care Plan, admission is dealt with through the statutory process rather than the standard admissions procedure.
If your child has an Education, Health and Care Plan, or you would like to discuss Drybrook’s provision for children with SEND before applying, please contact the school office at admin@dbp.fodt.co.uk.
Further information is available in the SEND section of this website.
Visiting Drybrook
We believe that visiting a school is one of the best ways to decide whether it is right for your child.
We are proud of Drybrook and would be delighted to show prospective families around the school. During your visit, you will have the opportunity to see our learning environment, meet members of our team and find out more about our curriculum, values and wider opportunities.
To arrange a visit, please contact the school office.
Our Admissions Policies
The formal admission arrangements and oversubscription criteria for Drybrook are contained in the relevant Admissions Policies below.
School Prospectus
You can find out more about life at Drybrook, including our curriculum, school day, uniform, pastoral support and opportunities for children, throughout this website.

Forest Food Bank
Before Christmas, the staff and children at Drybrook school collected for the Foodbank as a focus on giving in the Christmas season.
Drybrook school raised an amazing amount of food to donate to the food bank which helped supply around 148 meals for families in crisis at this time of year.
Well done and thank you to all who supported this worthy cause.

Forest of Dean Trust
The Forest of Dean Trust has a simple mission. We strive to continue improving our schools' outcomes and to play our role in affecting positive change in our communities. To do this, our schools collaborate in all areas and share best practices.
The Forest of Dean Trust is built upon excellent relationships, honest conversations and unwavering support to get the best out of each other. Staff work together to improve their teaching, students are actively involved in their school and parents are listened to and supported in our shared journey.
The modern world is a complex place and we seek to equip our students with the skills to thrive and to make a difference. We relish the opportunity we have been given to influence the lives of young people in the Forest of Dean. Our trust has a common-sense approach to working with young people that is founded on giving and getting respect. Our staff love their jobs, and we work hard to instill a love of school and community into our students. We are very serious about our role within the community and we are an active presence within it.
